proof_nl:
Let n>1 be an integer, let m be an integer with 0<=m<=n-1, and let t be a real number with m/n <= t < (m+1)/n. We prove that floor(n t) <= m.

Since n>1, we have n>0. Multiplying the inequality t < (m+1)/n by the positive number n gives n t < m+1.

By the definition of the floor function, floor(n t) is an integer and floor(n t) <= n t. Hence floor(n t) < m+1.

Because floor(n t) is an integer, the strict inequality floor(n t) < m+1 implies floor(n t) <= m. Therefore floor(n t) <= m, as required.
solver_summary: From t<(m+1)/n and n>0, obtain nt<m+1; since floor(nt) is an integer with floor(nt)≤nt, it follows that floor(nt)<m+1, hence floor(nt)≤m.
